questions.question: When would you use CSS Grid instead of Flexbox?
questions.title: Css Grid Vs Flexbox
questions.direct_answer: Grid for two-dimensional layouts — you design the row/column structure and place items into it (the container owns the layout). Flexbox for one-dimensional distribution — items flow along one axis and their sizes drive the result (the content owns the layout). Practical split: page shells, dashboards, image galleries, anything with aligned rows AND columns → Grid; navbars, toolbars, button groups, splitting a card into title/body/footer → Flexbox. They compose — Grid areas containing Flex components is the standard architecture.

```mermaid

    Q{Alignment across both axes?}
    Q -->|yes - rows and columns align| G[GRID: page shell, dashboard, gallery]
    Q -->|no - one axis is enough| F[FLEX: navbar, toolbar, card rows]
    subgraph composition
        P[Grid page] --> F2[Flex navbar inside]
        P --> G2[Grid card area inside]
        G2 --> F3[Flex card internals]
    end
```

sections.title: Deep Dive
sections.content:
The dimensional difference formalized (the mental model): Flexbox is a single flexible line (wrapping creates independent lines with no cross-line alignment). Grid is a track-based plane: template-columns and template-rows define named/numbered tracks, fr units distribute container space proportionally (1fr 2fr = 1:2 split), and minmax(min, 1fr) sets floors — `repeat(auto-fill, minmax(240px, 1fr))` is the famous responsive-card-grid WITHOUT media queries: as many 240px-min columns as fit, sharing space evenly.

The content-vs-container axis (the philosophy): Flexbox asked 'how do I distribute these?' — sizing flows FROM the items (basis, grow). Grid asks 'what structure am I?' — sizing flows from the TRACKS (fr, minmax) and items are placed INTO it. This is why Grid replaced float-hacks for page layout (floats were content-flow hacks) while Flexbox replaced inline-block hacks for component layout.

Placement models (the power difference): Grid offers line-based placement (grid-column: 2 / 4), named areas (grid-template-areas — the readable layout-as-diagram syntax), spanning (span 2), and overlap (two items in the same cells + z-index — the poster-child feature flex can't do). Subgrid (the 2023+ feature) lets nested grids inherit the parent's tracks — the fix for 'aligned card interiors' that previously forced flattening components into one grid.
